mstts:express-as.prosody:
As we wrap up, let’s take a moment to reflect on what really matters here.
Every single one of us is shaped by more than just the family or traditions we inherit—it's also about the choices we make along the way. Life’s not always a straight path. Sometimes, it’s messy, winding, and full of surprises. But through it all, humor and storytelling can be lifelines—ways to survive, to heal, and to push back against what tries to hold us down.
Facing pain honestly, with courage, and leaning on the people around us, that’s where true healing begins. And tradition? It’s not just about repeating the past. It’s alive. It grows and adapts, even as it honors where we’ve come from.
The greatest legacy anyone can leave isn’t about wealth or status—it’s about learning to see the world with respect and humility.
The journey of Lame Deer and the Lakota people shows us that no one’s story moves in a straight line. It’s full of hardship, laughter, loss, and hope. And those lessons—they’re not just for one group or one moment in history. They’re here for anyone searching for meaning in a world that’s often uncertain.
So, if you’re ever feeling stuck between old ways and new realities, or you’re struggling to heal wounds that seem just too deep, remember—you’re not alone in this. The wisdom of those who came before, the strength of community, and the power that lives inside your own story are always within reach.
Take time to listen. Make space for laughter. Seek out your own vision. And when you can, pass the fire forward.
By doing that, you’re not only honoring those who came before, but you’re opening the door to a future that can be better for everyone.
Here’s to carrying the story—and the hope—forward.
